entries.clue: Diver caught by current around hazardous sea feature? (7)

indicatorNotes.caught by: the diver is held by what follows it, so C and I come after GREBE

blocks.note: a grebe is a diving waterbird
c = caught, the cricket scorecard abbreviation
I is the symbol for electric current

annotation.surface: A diver is swept along by a current past some danger lurking in the sea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Diver' looks like a person in a wetsuit; it is the bird. The question mark flags that an iceberg is a hazard rather than a formal definition of one.
annotation.definitionFit: An iceberg is a floating mass of ice, a notorious danger to shipping.

entries.clue: Sanitise scalpel – as NHS vet regularly (7)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at regular intervals: every second one

blocks.note: the even letters of sCaLpEl aS nHsVeT

annotation.surface: Advice to sterilise surgical instruments the way a health-service vet would.
annotation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service; the dash and capitals are there only to make the letter string look like a sentence.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean freeing something of dirt or germs.

entries.clue: Practical joke – bash knocker – run the other way (5,4)

indicatorNotes.run the other way: the word before it is read backwards

blocks.note: knocker is slang for a breast, a boob

annotation.surface: A prank of hitting a door knocker and running off, like knock-down-ginger.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Knocker' suggests a door, but it is cheeky slang. The clue lists bash first, yet it is placed second in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A booby trap, like a bucket balanced on a door, is a classic practical joke.

entries.clue: Miles Pedro cycled went quickly, easily (6)

indicatorNotes.cycled: letters move from one end to the other, keeping their order

annotation.surface: A man called Pedro cycled many miles at an easy speed.
annotation.walkthrough: MPEDRO has its last two letters, RO, moved to the front. 'Cycled' reads as riding a bike but means rotating the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: To romp is to go along briskly and easily, as in romping home to win.

entries.clue: Architectural style of a road round middle of Acton Green (3,4)

indicatorNotes.round: RD goes round the next letter
indicatorNotes.middle of: take the central letter of Acton

annotation.surface: A question about the building style of a road near Acton Green in west London.
annotation.walkthrough: Acton Green is a real place in London, so the eye reads it as one name; it has to be split, with Green standing alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Art deco is the geometric 1920s-30s style seen in many cinemas and houses.

entries.clue: Dancer maybe needing control – Fred Astaire chose her conclusively (8)

indicatorNotes.conclusively: take the final letter of each word

blocks.note: to rein in is to control
last letters of freD astairE chosE heR

annotation.surface: A dancer needing firm guidance, like the partners Fred Astaire picked.
annotation.walkthrough: Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer, disguised by the capital that starts the sentence; Fred Astaire pushes us firmly towards ballrooms.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Dancer pulls Santa's sleigh alongside Dasher and Prancer, and the 'maybe' admits it.

entries.clue: Bad doctor starts practice (5)

indicatorNotes.starts: the doctor comes first, ahead of 'bad'

blocks.note: ill = bad, as in ill will

annotation.surface: An incompetent doctor sets up a practice of his own.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Practice' looks like a surgery; it is repeated exercise.
annotation.definitionFit: A drill is repeated practice, such as a fire drill.

entries.clue: Property Lawrence left following gossip (7)

indicatorNotes.following: TE and L come after the gossip

blocks.note: T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia

annotation.surface: A will dispute: Lawrence left some property after rumours spread.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like bequeathed; it is just L.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal term: movable personal possessions, as opposed to land, are chattels.

entries.clue: Bought smack – it’s not for everyone (8,5)

blocks.note: a smack of something is a taste of it

annotation.surface: Buying heroin is a habit only some people take up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Smack' is slang for heroin in the surface; here it is a trace of flavour.
annotation.definitionFit: An acquired taste is something only some people come to like.

entries.clue: Oddly looking in reflection of mirror, Freud reveals damage (6)

blocks.note: surface padding: the gaze into the mirror

annotation.surface: Freud gazing strangely at his reflection in a mirror, uncovering some psychological harm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Looking in' is the surface's glance into the mirror and does no work; the mirror both supplies letters and hints at the reversal.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: twisting something out of shape spoils or harms it.

entries.clue: Somehow I’m in car pound to complete fence? (8)

indicatorNotes.Somehow: the letters are arranged in some other way
indicatorNotes.to complete: what completes something comes last, so the pound finishes the word

blocks.note: l = pound, from the Latin libra

annotation.surface: Someone stuck in a car pound, trying to finish putting up a fence.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fence' looks like garden boundary work; it is a receiver of stolen goods, hence the question mark for an example.
annotation.definitionFit: A fence, who handles stolen goods, is one kind of criminal.

entries.clue: Palladium line-up announced without delay (3)

indicatorNotes.announced: the word is spoken, so we write what it sounds like

blocks.note: Pd is the chemical symbol for palladium
a queue is a line-up; said out loud it is the letter Q

annotation.surface: The cast list for the London Palladium theatre is revealed straight away.
annotation.walkthrough: The Palladium is a famous London theatre, so 'line-up' reads as a bill of acts.
annotation.definitionFit: PDQ, pretty damn quick, means immediately.

entries.clue: State of excitement after father leaves me stain remover? (6)

indicatorNotes.leaves: a father who leaves walks out, so his letters depart from FRENZY
indicatorNotes.after: what comes after follows, so the remainder of FRENZY is followed by ME

blocks.note: Fr = Father, a priest's title; it leaves FRENZY

annotation.surface: A child is thrilled when dad goes and leaves them to scrub a stain.
annotation.walkthrough: Biological washing powders use enzymes to break down stains, which the question mark admits is one use among many.
annotation.definitionFit: Enzymes in biological detergents break down stains, so an enzyme can be a stain remover.

entries.clue: Ripple of muscle with inappropriate squeezing (8)

blocks.note: lat = latissimus dorsi, the broad back muscle

annotation.surface: A muscle rippling, perhaps pinched awkwardly.
annotation.walkthrough: The container is read from the end: 'with inappropriate squeezing' means UNDUE squeezing the muscle.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: both describe a surface moving in small waves.

entries.clue: Show with lead for Dick Van Dyke, say (5)

blocks.note: to bear a mark or sign is to show it

annotation.surface: A show whose leading role goes to the actor Dick Van Dyke.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals make us read Dick Van Dyke, the actor; the definition steals only Van Dyke, a pointed beard named after the painter.
annotation.definitionFit: A Van Dyke is a short pointed beard, as in Van Dyck's portraits.

entries.clue: It’s hard to build on this level of martial arts proficiency (5,4)

annotation.definition: It’s hard to build on this

blocks.clueFragment: It’s hard to build on this

blocks.note: a coloured belt grade in judo or karate

annotation.surface: A pun joining planning rules with judo gradings.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain the green belt is protected countryside round a city where building is restricted.
annotation.definitionFit: Green belt land resists development, and a green belt is a mid-level martial arts grade.

entries.clue: Risk for one willing to go after directors (5,4)

blocks.note: game = willing, as in game for anything

annotation.surface: A daring person keen to chase company bosses is taking a risk.
annotation.walkthrough: Risk is the world-conquest board game, hidden by the capital at the start of the sentence.
annotation.definitionFit: Risk is a well-known board game, so an example of one.

entries.clue: These used to be wine and cheese consuming soirees originally (8)

indicatorNotes.consuming: what the cheese consumes ends up inside it, so AND sits within BRIE

blocks.note: brie is a soft French cheese

annotation.surface: Wine-and-cheese evening parties of the past, perhaps.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wine and cheese' reads as a pairing; only cheese is wordplay, while 'and' goes inside it literally. Brandy is distilled from wine.
annotation.definitionFit: Brandy is made by distilling wine, so brandies were once wine.

entries.clue: Camouflage-wearing soldier on first of these charts (3,6)

indicatorNotes.wearing: HIDE has the rest inside it like clothing
indicatorNotes.on: in an across answer, one thing on another is added onto its end, so PARA follows T

annotation.surface: A soldier in camouflage consults his maps before a mission.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charts' looks like military maps; it is the pop charts.
annotation.definitionFit: The hit parade is the list of best-selling records, the charts.

entries.clue: Mental pictures conjured up by this writer’s mature line (7)

annotation.surface: A mature line of verse by the author calls up vivid pictures.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Line' looks like a line of writing; it is a railway line.
annotation.definitionFit: Imagery is the mental pictures a piece of writing creates.

entries.clue: Dad and sister occasionally dated (5)

indicatorNotes.occasionally: only some letters, every other one, are taken

annotation.surface: A father and his sister went on the odd date.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dated' looks like going out romantically; it is old-fashioned.
annotation.definitionFit: Passé means out of date, no longer fashionable.

entries.clue: Language in exchange with Larkin – the poet – after losing pages (7)

indicatorNotes.after losing: once they have lost their pages, SWAP and PHILIP are left without their Ps

blocks.note: a swap is an exchange; P removed leaves SWA
the poet Philip Larkin; both Ps removed leaves HILI
p = page, so pages = the Ps lost

annotation.surface: A language exchange with the poet Larkin, after the manuscript lost some pages.
annotation.walkthrough: Larkin needs his first name, Philip, before the deletion leaves anything useful.
annotation.definitionFit: Swahili is a Bantu language widely spoken in East Africa.

entries.clue: Lady Gaga finally appearing in fashion mag – not everyone can see this passage (6)

indicatorNotes.finally: the last letter of each word
indicatorNotes.appearing in: a star appearing in a magazine is printed inside it, so YA goes within the magazine's letters
indicatorNotes.not everyone can see this: the U film certificate, suitable for all, is removed

blocks.note: U = universal, the British film certificate for all ages; it is dropped

annotation.surface: Lady Gaga features in a glossy magazine in a restricted article.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain a U-rated film is suitable for everyone, so 'not everyone' removes a U from VOGUE.
annotation.definitionFit: A passage is a journey, especially by sea: a voyage.

entries.clue: Last of flight crew joining when international airport’s opening in part of Australia (8)

indicatorNotes.joining: the pieces are joined in order

annotation.surface: The final flight crew board an international plane heading to an Australian state.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crew' looks like the flight crew as a noun; it is the verb man.
annotation.definitionFit: Tasmania is the island state south of mainland Australia.

entries.clue: A male issue undermining biggest character of Matthew Perry on TV? (5)

indicatorNotes.undermining: in a down answer, A SON sits beneath M
indicatorNotes.biggest character of: the first, capital letter of Matthew

blocks.note: Matthew starts with a capital M
a son is male offspring, issue

annotation.surface: A question about Matthew Perry's best-known role, Chandler in the TV sitcom Friends.
annotation.walkthrough: Matthew Perry the Friends actor is a decoy; the definition takes only Perry, meaning Perry Mason, the TV lawyer.
annotation.definitionFit: Perry Mason is the defence lawyer of the long-running TV series.

entries.clue: Former bowler, possibly 21 (3-3)

blocks.note: old = former, as in an old flame

annotation.surface: A retired cricket bowler, perhaps now past it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' looks like a cricketer; it is a hard round hat. The definition points at 21 across, PASSE.
annotation.definitionFit: Old hat means out of date, just like passé.

entries.clue: Throw pipe down next to yard (3)

indicatorNotes.next to: things next to each other sit side by side, so Y is written straight after SH

blocks.note: sh! means be quiet, pipe down

annotation.surface: An order to toss a pipe down into the garden.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pipe down' reads as a length of piping being lowered; it is the command to be quiet.
annotation.definitionFit: A less common verb sense, surviving in the coconut shy, a fairground stall where balls are thrown at coconuts.

entries.clue: Top 30 without The White Stripes ultimately taking year out (3-5)

indicatorNotes.without: THIRT goes outside the other letters
indicatorNotes.ultimately: the last letter of each word
indicatorNotes.taking: to take something out is to remove it, so the year is extracted from THIRTY
indicatorNotes.out: completes 'taking out': the year ends up out of the word

blocks.note: y = year; it is taken out, leaving THIRT
last letters of thE whitE stripeS

annotation.surface: A top-thirty chart missing the band The White Stripes, who have stepped away for a year.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top 30' looks like a chart and the 30 like a cross-reference to 30 across; it is just the number.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: in clothing talk a top is any upper-body garment, and a tee-shirt is one.

entries.clue: See you in Ibiza, when snorting a gram, son must go slowly (6)

indicatorNotes.when snorting: the word takes A G inside it
indicatorNotes.must go: someone who must go has to leave, so the son's S departs from ADIOS

blocks.note: adiós is Spanish for goodbye; Ibiza is Spanish

annotation.surface: A drug warning for holidaymakers in Ibiza: your son should ease off.
annotation.walkthrough: The drug surface hides a music term; 'go slowly' is not the definition, since 'must go' is the deletion.
annotation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical direction meaning slowly.

entries.clue: Just soybean spread (2,1,4)

indicatorNotes.spread: the letters are spread out and rearranged

annotation.surface: Nothing but a spread made from soya beans.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'only'; it means barely, as a horse wins by a nose.
annotation.definitionFit: To win by a nose is to win only just.

entries.clue: Torment two bases (7)

blocks.note: a bed is a base, as a flower bed or foundation
base means low and wicked: evil

annotation.walkthrough: 'Bases' is used twice in different senses: a foundation noun, then the adjective base meaning immoral.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to harass someone persistently, as if by a devil.
